They are distinct from signatures over the exact whole server-created commit, whose creation timestamps are not independently predictable, and from a complete release/build provenance chain.
claim_ceiling: Policy-scoped integrity between the client-confirmed deterministic intent record and checked commit fields under key/client/cryptographic assumptions, supporting L4 source-history evidence. Signatures are necessary to authenticate the record; bare hashes would not replace them. This does not establish real-person identity, current release authority, license permission, harmless source semantics, complete history availability or source-to-APK correctness.
source_basis: Retrieved PDF pp. 1-14 (complete retrieved representation including references and included appendices); field-specific sections and pages in field_evidence.csv; Fourteen-page author-hosted ASIACCS2018 layout, le-git-imate: Towards Verifiable Web-based Git Repositories, DOI10.1145/3196494.3196523. title: Contour: A Practical System for Binary Transparency
evidence_object: Batched binary-hash Merkle commitments anchored in an authority's signed Bitcoin transactions, with inclusion proofs checked against the auditor's independently maintained block-header view. Optional archivists mirror binary data; monitors inspect it using methods expressly outside Contour's scope. Publication commitment, data retention and inspection are separate properties.
claim_ceiling: Authenticated evidence that an authority's binary commitment was included in an agreed ledger view, with conditional availability if trustworthy archivists retain corresponding data. This can strengthen publication-history evidence but alone establishes neither complete L4 source/build provenance nor L5 release permission, actual monitor approval, harmless L6 behavior or semantic equivalence. The source's comparison table explicitly notes that CoSi's constant auditor cost is not a global-log inclusion cost and that availability depends on retention.

title: Do Users Write More Insecure Code with AI Assistants?
evidence_object: IRB-approved controlled human programming study using an author-built Codex interface. Fifty-four recruited participants become47after exclusions:33assistant-access and14control, with random assignment targeted2:1 and randomized task order. Six tasks were offered; one browser-display task was dropped after the study as too vague, leaving five analyzed tasks across Python, JavaScript and C. Most participants are students and the setting is a two-hour lab task, not production Android development.
claim_ceiling: Conditional evidence of different solution security and self-reported confidence under this assistant-access treatment, task set, scoring policy and sample. Four tasks have descriptively less-secure assisted outcomes, while the C task is mixed; results do not establish that all assistance always increases harm. This study does not authenticate training membership, copying history, full L4 build provenance, L5 authorization or security of a deployed application. It credits the different model/task setting of Sandoval et al. rather than treating the findings as interchangeable.
